title: SEC0: unknown comparator silently accepted instead of failing per RFC 5228
description:
RFC 5228 §2.7.2 states: 'If a comparator name is unknown, the implementation MUST fail the script.' Currently, unknown comparators like ':comparator "i;invalid"' silently fall back to 'i;ascii-casemap' (the default) instead of causing the match test to fail or the script compilation to fail.

Location: crates/sieve-native/src/evaluator.rs, extract_comparator() function (lines 307-333)

Current behavior:
- Line 318: if s == "i;octet" { cmp = Comparator::Octet; }
- If the comparator string doesn't match "i;octet", it remains as the default AsciiCasemap
- This allows scripts with unknown comparators to compile and execute with wrong semantics

Correct behavior per RFC 5228:
- Unknown comparators should cause the script to fail (either at compile time or cause the match test to return false)

Severity: P2
- Only affects scripts with non-standard/invalid comparators
- Well-formed Sieve scripts only use the two standard comparators: 'i;ascii-casemap' and 'i;octet'
- Both are correctly implemented
- Cross-validation tests pass because the oracle (sieve-rs) may have the same behavior

Test coverage: No tests currently cover unknown comparators
